posts.title: Day 12 of Cop31 – recapped
posts.text: That’s all for today. Here are the highlights from the 12th day of the 31st UN climate summit, which has now run into overtime: African negotiators accused rich countries of undermining the credibility of Cop by failing to provide needed cash Civil society activists called Antalya 2026 the ‘worst Cop ever’ Small…

China appears to have endorsed the flagship 35x35 electrification pledge, as momentum gathers behind at least of the key goals of this summit. In a joint statement with Australia, published by the state-run Xinhua news agency, the two countries said they welcome “growing international ambition and cooperation on…

My colleague Gabrielle Canon and I have been speaking to people at Cop31 about carbon capture technology. Saudi Arabia is understood to be among the countries pushing for Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS) to be strongly referenced in a final agreement being negotiated by more than 190 countries at the UN…
What does the draft text say – and, perhaps more importantly, what does it really mean? My colleague Fiona Harvey has expertly broken down the key points of the jargon-filled document here.
The Guardian understands there will probably now not be a new draft of the agreement for negotiators to pore over until Saturday morning.

‘Too often, finance moves slower than floods’ Every day for the two weeks of Cop31 I’ve been speaking to young climate activists. Today I spoke to Sidra Riaz, 29, from Pakistan. In 2022, she founded Environmental Change Makers, a youth-led climate education initiative, during the devastating Pakistan floods of 2022.…

We do now have a bit more clarity on what’s happening here. The closing plenary is going to start at 8pm Antalya time, but this is just to close off items that have been negotiated already. Countries may or may not get a new draft text to mull over tonight, but this is going to go to Saturday. The plenary should also…

There’s been a noticeable shift in the energy among journalists here in the media centre at Cop31 since it became clear we were not going to finish on time. This should be a shock to nobody. The last time a Cop did finish on time – if we take 6pm as the end of the day – was Italy in 2003, according to Carbon Brief. So…

Our friends at Carbon Brief have shared the results of a sweepstake to guess when the gavel will finally come down to signal the end of the summit. The median estimate is 10.35pm on Saturday (local time), which would be more than one full day after the scheduled finish. The most pessimistic answer is Tuesday…

The conference has now entered overtime. As diplomats haggle over the precise words in the final text, it can be easy to lose sight of what the world stands to lose from a failure to act. Beneath the jargon, it is real people’s lives – including your own – that are at stake. A few weeks ago, I spoke to a French doctor…
